name: Bandai Bridge
connectingPointsDisplay: Niigata Station — South side of the Shinano River
facts: Bandai Bridge, completed in 1929, stretches 306.9 meters across the Shinano River, its six reinforced‑concrete arches surviving a 1964 7.5‑magnitude earthquake that toppled most other bridges in Niigata.

The bridge’s granite‑sided façade and 21.9‑meter width earned it 2004 designation as a nationally Important Cultural Property, marking it as Niigata’s iconic symbol and a nightly illuminated landmark.
During the 1948 Niigata Festival, a fireworks mishap on Bandai Bridge sent over 100 spectators into the river, prompting a lasting ban on fireworks displays across all Shinano River bridges.
